title: Rogue DB-10 DB-15 loadable dumbbells review - Best on the market?
summary: He reviews Rogue's DB-10 and DB-15 loadable dumbbells after a year of use. They are expensive but nearly indestructible and save space; the main differences are collar length and maximum load, and loaded plates change the feel and strength curve.
claims: A pair of fixed dumbbells is cheap, but a full set covering shoulders, biceps and triceps costs a few thousand, which is why adjustable dumbbells make sense
He keeps no machines or racks in his gym because they take too much space and cannot be moved
DB-10 and DB-15 have identical handle length and knurling, moderately aggressive and similar to the Rogue Ohio Power Bar; chrome finish does not change the grip
Collar length is the only real difference between the two models
The DB-10 weighs 10 lb and fits two standard 10 lb plates plus the collar, for about 55-60 lb maximum safely
The DB-15 weighs 15 lb and fits five 10 lb plates per side plus the collar, up to about 115 lb
Leave room for the collar; if plates press directly on it, it will work loose
A fully loaded DB-15 is long enough that plates hit your body on curls; he had to switch dumbbell rows from inside to outside his body
They are extremely durable, surviving drops on steel and stone; only the logo marking wears off
DB-10s cost about 80 dollars or more and DB-15s over 100 each
Worth it if you do 4-6 isolation movements a week at different weights, arm wrestle, or are too strong for most dumbbells on rows; not worth it for occasional isolation
Loadable dumbbells are bulkier than fixed ones of the same weight and have a different strength curve, so start light to avoid injury
exercises: row outside the body with long loaded dumbbells
